purpose: Reconstruct and provenance-bind only the released Planck pressure correlation structure for the eight already-exposed X-COP development clusters, while recording why pressure, temperature, density, calibration, background, beam/PSF, and cross-instrument covariance gates remain incomplete.

public_metadata.audited_fact: The official X-COP page distributes high-level thermodynamic profiles and a complete downloadable data archive for the named X-COP clusters.
The primary X-COP thermodynamic analysis documents spatially resolved density, temperature, and Planck pressure profiles for the X-COP sample.

pressure_covariance_reconstruction.mapping_rule: Verify identical bin order through constant radius and central-profile scale ratios, convert the released COVMAT to a correlation matrix, then apply the already-used standalone physical pressure errors as C_target=diag(eP_SZ*P500) Corr_released diag(eP_SZ*P500).
pressure_covariance_reconstruction.mapping_reason: The covariance product and standalone Item 59 profile use the same bin order but different constant radius/profile normalizations; retaining the released correlation structure and the scorer's existing diagonal errors avoids inventing a unit conversion or silently changing the scored central values.

auxiliary_inventory.interpretation: The archive contains processed background/exposure/science mosaics and marginal spectral summaries, but not the event-level, response, PSF-mixing, noise-realisation, mask, or calibration files needed to reconstruct X-ray radial or cross-instrument covariance.

CP5.1.reconstructible: Eight development-cluster Planck pressure correlation matrices, diagonal-calibrated to the already-scored standalone pressure errors.
CP5.1.blocker: The reconstructed matrices are not yet wired into a frozen scorer, do not separate beam/background/deprojection components, and do not cover an independent source packet.
CP5.1.smallest_next_action: Run a no-refit development-only diagonal-versus-reconstructed-pressure-covariance score comparison and publish every per-cluster score delta.

CP5.2.reconstructible: Only released per-bin X-ray temperature errors and asymmetric spectral-fit intervals.
CP5.2.blocker: No temperature likelihood surface, posterior samples, cross-bin covariance, ARF/RMF, or shared calibration realization is present.
CP5.2.smallest_next_action: Request or reproduce one development-cluster annular spectral likelihood with response and background files before generalizing.

CP5.3.blocker: No surface-brightness count covariance, deprojection operator covariance, PSF mixing matrix, or density Monte Carlo ensemble is present.
CP5.3.smallest_next_action: Reconstruct one development-cluster density covariance from public counts, exposure, background, and a frozen deprojection/PSF operator.

CP5.4.reconstructible: A declared global 0.9/1.0/1.1 X-ray temperature cross-calibration sensitivity grid, which is a model stress test rather than measured covariance.
CP5.4.blocker: No shared XMM-temperature/Planck-pressure calibration covariance or joint calibration samples are present.
CP5.4.smallest_next_action: Freeze an externally calibrated shared nuisance prior and its channel-loading matrix before any covariance-aware score.

CP5.5.reconstructible: Processed XMM background/exposure mosaics and Planck covariance metadata with a 7.3 arcmin beam, 1001 simulations, and 10000 Monte Carlo draws.
CP5.5.blocker: The actual Planck simulations and beam/mask products, plus XMM event lists, PSF, ARF/RMF, background-component realizations, and reduction configuration are absent.
CP5.5.smallest_next_action: Bind the raw realization and response files for one development cluster and replay the published radial extraction exactly.

CP5.6.reconstructible: No cross-instrument covariance; only separate channel summaries and the uncalibrated global sensitivity grid.
CP5.6.blocker: No XMM-Chandra comparison packet and no X-ray/SZ joint calibration covariance are bound.
CP5.6.smallest_next_action: Construct a named shared-nuisance design matrix from an external calibration sample, retaining instrument-specific and common modes separately.
